correctness.rationale: Exact cyclotomic divisibility proves F_A(u)=0 iff each residue 0,+/-u_j occurs once. Signed coordinate normalization and the graph construction are reversible. The actual packaged Python checker enumerates every normalized candidate and every maximal clique with an exhaustive recursive algorithm; profiles establish a unique clique of the full required cardinality at all four stated primes. Spectrum counts follow by elementary line/coset counting; a separate modular assertion checks the p13 local witness. Nothing is extrapolated beyond the finite domain.

originality.rationale: The four-prime all-spectrum classification and exact counts require the complete normalized clique profiles. General spectral-to-weak-tiling and Gabor-pair results, and Fourier-zero ray closure, do not imply global clique uniqueness. The thirteen-field noncollinear partial orthogonality demonstrates that a simple local-collinearity deduction cannot replace the new global certificate. Targeted primary-literature and published-finding corpus comparisons found no dominating statement; explicit archival-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A prior Lee-cross, complete-mapping, complex Hadamard, or perfect-code enumeration might present an equivalent four-prime classification under different language despite the actual targeted searches.

value.rationale: All spectra of a canonical p-point radius-one Lee cross form a natural exact Fourier invariant, not a made-up slice: the first four nontrivial primes and their four full spectra counts are completely classified. At p13 a compatible noncollinear partial orthogonal family exists despite line-only complete bases, giving a meaningful global rigidity boundary and a benchmark for finite spectral set and coding questions. Neither mere spectrum existence nor numerical reproducibility alone constitutes the claimed value.
